# Fabcheck — Opt-In and CI Enforcement

How to wire fabcheck into a project as an opt-in `make fabcheck` target and CI
workflow.

> Tool internals (language coverage, dist-name resolution modes, known gaps,
> verdict.json shape) live in
> [knowledgebase/build/fabcheck.md](https://github.com/jewzaam/knowledgebase/blob/main/build/fabcheck.md).

## Opting in

1. Copy [templates/fabcheck.mk](templates/fabcheck.mk) to `make/fabcheck.mk`
   in your project.
2. Copy [templates/fabcheck.sh](templates/fabcheck.sh) to `scripts/fabcheck.sh`.
3. Add to your Makefile:

   ```makefile
   -include make/fabcheck.mk
   ```

4. Copy [templates/workflows/fabcheck.yml](templates/workflows/fabcheck.yml) to
   `.github/workflows/` for CI enforcement.

Fabcheck is **not** part of `check`. It runs explicitly via `make fabcheck` or
in CI. This matches the convention for opt-in targets like `version-check` and
`mutation`.

## CI integration

The reference CI workflow runs `make install-dev` before `make fabcheck` so
the active venv has the project's declared deps installed. This flips the
Python resolver into `precise` mode — see the knowledgebase counterpart for
the modes table.

## Tests

Fabcheck itself is tested by fixture scenarios in
[../tests/fabcheck/](../tests/fabcheck/README.md). Run with `make test-fabcheck`
in this repo.
